mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 250,000 in a month indicates strong labor market conditions, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 250,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which often leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strong supply side, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by less than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS growth is less than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month, it signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% YoY, it indicates a tightening monetary policy in response to inflationary pressure, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL is above 2%.
